title: Talk to Your Sheriff Meeting
description:
Join our small interfaith group of clergy and local community members to meet with our sheriff and make a community-led moral ask for them to decline to cooperate with ICE.

Sheriffs nationwide are being pushed into cooperating with ICE in three main ways. ICE requests sheriffs to:
- Rent bed space in jails that Sheriffs operate to ICE.
- Hold people for an additional 48 hours so that ICE can pick them up. 
- Sign a 287g - a document which allows local law enforcement to have the authority of ICE agents and enforce civil warrants that pop up in NCIC (the police database).

**We have a simple message to our sheriff: This is a moment that demands moral clarity.** They do not have to do ICE’s job. When sheriffs take on the responsibility of federal immigration authorities, it undermines their core mission, stretches already limited resources, and most importantly, causes real harm.

Join our conversation and represent yourself or your congregation. Your moral voice is of value. We are in the process of scheduling with the sheriff's office, but once you RSVP we will be in touch with scheduling details.

title: Black August Film & Discussion: Reckoning with Racial Terror and Displacement in U.S. History
description:
This Black August, we invite you to gather with us for a screening and discussion of two powerful films that confront the legacy of racial violence and displacement in the United States.

We'll begin with An Outrage (34 min), a short documentary filmed on-site at lynching locations across the American South. Through the voices of descendants, scholars, and community members, the film sheds light on the thousands of African Americans murdered by white mobs in acts of state-sanctioned racial terror. It asks us not only to remember this long-silenced history but to take action to honor those lost and the communities that resisted.

Our second screening will be Banished (84 min), which traces the violent expulsion of Black communities from hundreds of U.S. counties between 1860 and 1920. The film examines how these racial cleansings shattered families, stole land, and erased Black presence in entire regions, while raising hard questions about reconciliation, reparations, and what justice might look like today.

Together, these films offer critical insight into the systems of racial violence that have shaped this country and that continue to reverberate in the present.

After the screenings, we’ll hold an open conversation about the themes raised, the history often omitted from mainstream narratives, and the ways we can engage in resistance and solidarity today.

This event is part of our ongoing commitment to honor Black August—a time of study, reflection, and remembrance rooted in the struggle for Black liberation and political self-determination.

description:
Meet on the Meade Ave bridge over I-805. 

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.
